dublinCore.title: Compressed Sensing: Recovering a Sparse Spectrum
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Compressed sensing
Sparse recovery
Orthogonal matching pursuit
Sampling theorem
Aliasing
dublinCore.description: A real signal of N = 128 samples made of k tones is measured at only m sample times. Orthogonal matching pursuit (OMP) recovers its sparse spectrum from the m samples, while the minimum-energy (least-squares) solution spreads the energy over all frequencies. Sliders set k, m and the measurement noise; a menu compares random with evenly spaced sample times, which alias. Read-outs give both recovery errors, whether the support was recovered, the m >= C k ln(N/k) rule and the success rate over 100 fixed seeds.
relation: Chapter 14: Time-Frequency Analysis and Advanced Topics

searchKeywords: recover sparse spectrum from few samples

topic: Sparse recovery with orthogonal matching pursuit
learningObjectives: Explain why m random samples can recover a k-tone spectrum whose tones lie far above m/2 Hz, while m evenly spaced samples alias
Analyze one run of OMP (correlate, select, least squares, update the residual) and relate its first pick to the tallest bar of the minimum-energy spectrum
Compare the minimum-energy (least-squares) solution with the OMP solution using recovery error and sparsity
Evaluate the rule m >= C k ln(N/k) against the success rates measured over 100 seeds, and estimate C for OMP
Assess how measurement noise changes the recovery error and the support, and how extra measurements compensate
prerequisites: The DFT, its inverse and the conjugate symmetry of a real signal's spectrum
Least squares for an overdetermined linear system

misconceptions.misconception: Compressed sensing beats the sampling theorem for any signal
misconceptions.correction: Recovery from few samples needs a sparse spectrum; the number of samples must grow roughly like k ln(N/k)
misconceptions.evidence: With k = 10 and m = 32 only 1 of 100 seeds is recovered; with m = 64 all 100 are

misconceptions.misconception: Taking fewer samples is the same as sampling at a lower uniform rate
misconceptions.correction: Evenly spaced samples alias: DFT columns f and f +/- m become identical, so OMP cannot tell a tone from its alias; random sample times keep every column distinct
misconceptions.evidence: Seed 1, k = 3, m = 32: evenly spaced times make OMP return the aliases 10 and 8 Hz (2 of 100 seeds recovered) while random times recover 99 of 100 seeds

accessibility.screenReaderScript: Compressed sensing demonstration. A signal made of k cosines is measured at only m of its 128 sample times. The top plot shows the signal, the measured samples and the orthogonal matching pursuit reconstruction. The middle plot shows the spectrum of the minimum-energy (least-squares) solution, spread over all frequencies, and the bottom plot shows the sparse spectrum recovered by OMP with the true tones as rings. Read-outs give the recovery errors, whether the support was recovered, the m >= C k ln(N/k) rule and the success rate over 100 seeds.

controls.description: Moves to the next seed: new tones, new random sample times and new noise

visualElements.description: Signal x(t) over 1 s (blue), the m measured samples (orange dots and ticks) and the OMP estimate (green)
Amplitude spectrum (0 to 64 Hz) of the minimum-energy (least-squares) solution as maroon bars, with blue markers at the true tone frequencies
OMP spectrum: green stems at correct frequencies, red stems at wrong ones, blue rings at the true tones, and a dashed line at m/2 Hz
Banner and read-outs: OMP picks, support recovered, recovery errors, the m >= C k ln(N/k) rule and the success rate over seeds 1 to 100

model.description: A real k-sparse spectrum (k conjugate pairs of DFT bins) is measured at m sample times, y = Phi x_f + noise, with Phi the m rows of the inverse DFT matrix. OMP (k iterations, conjugate pairs added together) and the minimum-energy solution are computed and compared with the truth.
equations: x[n] = sum_{i=1}^{k} a_i cos(2 pi f_i n / N + phi_i), N = 128
c(f) = |sum_i r_i e^(-j 2 pi f t_i / N)|
minimum-energy solution: Phi^H (Phi Phi^H)^(-1) y = DFT of the zero-filled samples
rule of thumb: m >= C k ln(N/k), C about 2 to 4
algorithms: Orthogonal matching pursuit with least squares by incremental Gram-Schmidt QR
Seeded mulberry32 random generator with Box-Muller Gaussian noise

instructionalStrategies: Lower m until recovery fails and read the 100-seed success rate
Switch between random and evenly spaced sample times at the same m
Raise the noise and compensate with more samples
extensions: Add l1 minimization (basis pursuit) and compare it with OMP
Allow tones between DFT bins to show that leakage breaks exact sparsity
